    StartersVince's double cheese sliders with friesVince says try Fatburger from now on. Double beef, American cheese, onion, skinny fries.How to make it400g beef mince8 soft slider buns8 slices of American cheese1/2 white onion, finely diced8 dill pickle slices3 tbsp tomato sauce1 tbsp American mustard600g potatoes, cut in skinny fries1 L vegetable oil, for fryingFry the potatoes at 160°C until soft, drain, then fry again at 190°C until crisp and salt them.Roll the mince into 16 small balls, smash thin on a hot griddle and season.Flip, top half the patties with cheese and stack a plain one on each.Build in the toasted buns with onion, pickle, sauce and mustard and serve with the fries.Cha Cha Cha jerk chicken skewers with mangoMia's pick: the place with little red candles. Allspice and chilli chicken, grilled mango, lime.How to make it600g chicken thigh fillets, cubed3 spring onions, chopped1 red chilli2 garlic cloves1 tsp ground allspice1 tsp dried thyme2 tbsp soy sauce1 tbsp brown sugar2 limes1 mango, cut in chunks8 bamboo skewers, soakedBlend the spring onions, chilli, garlic, allspice, thyme, soy, sugar and the juice of a lime to a paste.Toss the chicken in the paste and leave for at least 10 minutes, or overnight.Thread the chicken and mango onto the skewers.Grill over high heat, turning, until charred and cooked through, and serve with lime wedges.Pickle from the jar on the counterMia rings it up with the tuna.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.SandwichesToretto's tuna on white, no crustBrian orders it every single day. Tuna, celery, dill pickle, lemon mayo, iceberg.How to make it8 slices of soft white bread2 x 185g tins of tuna in olive oil, drained2 celery sticks, finely diced2 dill pickles, finely diced4 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 lemon4 iceberg lettuce leaves1 tbsp chopped dillFlake the tuna into a bowl and mix with the celery, pickle, mayonnaise, dill, a little lemon zest and juice, salt and lots of pepper.Spread the tuna thickly over 4 slices of bread, add a lettuce leaf and close with the other slices.Press down gently, cut the crusts off with a sharp knife, then cut each sandwich in half.Quarter-mile Cuban pressed sandwichDom lives life a quarter mile at a time. Mojo pork, ham, Swiss, pickles, mustard, pressed.How to make it4 long crusty bread rolls800g boneless pork shoulder2 oranges2 limes4 garlic cloves, crushed1 tsp ground cumin1 tsp dried oregano150g sliced leg ham8 slices of Swiss cheese8 dill pickle slices3 tbsp American mustard30g butter, softenedMix the orange and lime juice with the garlic, cumin, oregano and 2 teaspoons of salt and rub it over the pork.Roast covered at 160°C until tender, then uncover for the last 20 minutes to brown, and rest.Slice the pork thinly, split the rolls and spread with mustard.Layer the ham, pork, cheese and pickles, butter the outsides and press in a hot pan under a heavy pan, turning once, until crisp and melting.Cut on the diagonal and serve.From the CaseTen-second churros with Mexican chocolateBrian owes Dom a ten-second car. Cinnamon sugar churros, thick spiced chocolate.How to make it250ml water60g butter1 tbsp caster sugar, plus 80g for coating150g plain flour2 eggs2 tsp ground cinnamon1 L vegetable oil, for frying150g dark chocolate, chopped250ml milk1/4 tsp chilli powderBring the water, butter and a tablespoon of sugar to the boil, tip in the flour and beat until it forms a ball, then cool for 5 minutes.Beat in the eggs one at a time and spoon the dough into a piping bag with a star nozzle.Warm the milk, stir in the chocolate, half the cinnamon and the chilli until thick and smooth.Pipe 12cm lengths into oil at 180°C and fry until golden, a few at a time.Roll the hot churros in the 80g sugar mixed with the rest of the cinnamon and serve with the chocolate.From the FridgeCorona with a wedge of limeAny brew you want, as long as it's a Corona. Ice cold, straight from the backyard tub.How to make it4 x 355ml bottles of Corona Extra1 lime, cut in wedges4 cups iceBury the bottles in a tub of ice for an hour.Open, push a lime wedge into each neck and hand them round.Ice-cold horchataFrom the market fridge, by the register.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
